answer: A spot-audit lottery prices each fake identity. A new identity posts a 40-credit bond and climbs a low knoll of probation with three honest jobs. Each epoch, 5 percent are drawn for an audit that bridges claimed work to on-chain receipts signed by that identity's key; failure burns the bond and freezes it for three epochs. History rental fails, since one rented history cannot bridge two identities. The kth fake still needs a fresh bond, jobs, and history, so 1,000 fakes risk 40,000 credits, while one honest identity posts 40 once and reaches the summit of reward weight.
